title: Have You Ever ...?
goals: menceritakan **pengalaman**: [[I have visited Bali.]], [[Have you ever eaten durian?]]

lesson.text: "Kamu **pernah** ke Bali?" "Aku **sudah** mengerjakan PR." "Aku **sudah lama** tinggal di sini." Semua ini memakai **present perfect**, tense yang menghubungkan **masa lalu dan sekarang**. Inilah topik **Unit 5 Kelas 9**.

lesson.title: 1. Rumus present perfect
lesson.text: Rumus: **have / has + past participle** (kata kerja bentuk ketiga, yang sudah kamu pelajari di Unit 3).

examples.en: Negatif: [[I haven't seen that movie.]] / [[He hasn't called me.]]
Pertanyaan: [[Have you eaten?]] — [[Yes, I have.]] / [[No, I haven't.]]

lesson.title: Singkatan
lesson.text: **I have = I've**, **she has = she's**, **have not = haven't**, **has not = hasn't**. Contoh: [[I've finished.]] / [[She hasn't come.]]

lesson.title: 2. Kapan memakai present perfect?
table: [[I have lived here for five years.]]
Aku sudah tinggal di sini lima tahun.

lesson.title: 3. Ever, never, already, yet, just
table: [[I haven't finished yet.]] / [[Have you eaten yet?]]

lesson.title: Never bukan haven't never
lesson.text: **Never** sudah bermakna negatif, jadi jangan ditambah not. Benar: [[I have never been to Bali.]] Salah: *I haven't never been to Bali.*

lesson.title: 4. For dan since
table: [[I have studied English for three years.]] / [[for two hours]], [[for a long time]]
[[I have studied English since 2023.]] / [[since Monday]], [[since I was ten]]

examples.en: [[How long have you lived here?]] — [[I have lived here for ten years.]]
examples.id: Sudah berapa lama kamu tinggal di sini? — Sudah sepuluh tahun.

lesson.title: 5. Present perfect atau simple past?
lesson.text: Perbedaannya: simple past memakai **waktu selesai yang jelas**; present perfect **tidak menyebut waktu** atau menghubungkan ke sekarang.
table: jelas dan sudah lewat (yesterday, last year, in 2020)
[[I have visited Bali.]] / [[I have visited Bali three times.]]

lesson.title: Tidak boleh dengan waktu lampau yang jelas
lesson.text: Jangan pakai present perfect bersama **yesterday**, **last week**, **in 2020**, atau **ago**. Benar: [[I saw him yesterday.]] Salah: *I have seen him yesterday.*

lines.en: Dina, have you ever been to Bali?
lines.id: Dina, apakah kamu pernah ke Bali?

lines.en: Yes, I have. I've been there twice. And you?
lines.id: Ya, pernah. Aku sudah ke sana dua kali. Kamu?

lines.en: No, I haven't. I've never been to Bali, but I've visited Yogyakarta.
lines.id: Belum. Aku belum pernah ke Bali, tapi aku pernah ke Yogyakarta.

lines.en: When did you go to Yogyakarta?
I went there last year. I have lived in Indonesia for three years now.
lines.id: Aku ke sana tahun lalu. Aku sudah tinggal di Indonesia tiga tahun sekarang.

read.text:
Rani: Have you ever been abroad, Budi?
Budi: Yes, I have. I have been to Singapore twice. I went there with my family in 2019 and 2022. Have you ever been there?
Rani: No, I haven't. I have never flown in a plane. But I have visited Bali by ship. I have always wanted to see the Merlion in Singapore.
read.title: Have You Ever Been Abroad?

read.id:
Aku sudah membaca lebih dari dua puluh novel tahun ini. Favoritku adalah cerita detektif. Aku sudah menamatkannya tiga kali! Aku juga bergabung dengan klub buku sejak Maret, dan aku sudah mendapat banyak teman baru di sana.
Bulan lalu, aku tidak bisa banyak membaca karena sibuk dengan ujian. Tetapi aku sudah merencanakan membaca novel fantasi baru selama liburan.

qs.q: How many novels has the writer read this year?

qs.exp: Teks: "My favorite is a detective story."
qs.q: What is the writer's favorite novel?
Since when has the writer joined the book club?
Why couldn't the writer read much last month?

read.text:
I have read more than twenty novels this year. My favorite is a detective story. I have finished it three times! I have also joined a book club since March, and I have made many new friends there.
Last month, I could not read much because I was busy with exams. But I have already planned to read a new fantasy novel during the holiday.
read.title: My Reading Experience

read.id:
Aku sudah mengunjungi banyak tempat di Indonesia. Aku sudah ke Bali tiga kali, dan aku sudah melihat candi-candi indah di Yogyakarta. Aku belum pernah ke Papua, tetapi aku selalu ingin pergi.
Temanku Tom sudah bepergian ke luar negeri. Dia sudah tinggal di Singapura selama dua tahun, dan dia sudah mengunjungi Jepang dua kali. Aku belum pernah ke luar negeri, tetapi aku sudah menabung untuk perjalanan pertamaku.

qs.exp: Teks: "I have been to Bali three times".
options: Once, when she was a small child
Never, because she doesn't like beaches
qs.q: How many times has the writer been to Bali?

qs.exp: Teks: "has lived in Singapore for two years".
qs.q: How long has Tom lived in Singapore?

qs.exp: Pengalaman tanpa waktu pasti → present perfect.
options: The experience is important now, and the time is not stated.
It happened yesterday, so the time is already finished.
It will happen tomorrow, so it is a plan.
It is a habit, so it happens every day.
qs.q: Why is the present perfect used for "I have been to Bali"?
Pasangkan kata kerja dengan past participle:
Tom ___ (live) in Singapore for two years.

qs.answer: I have never been to Papua.
qs.q: Susun kalimat dari cerita: "Aku belum pernah ke Papua."

read.text:
I have visited many places in Indonesia. I have been to Bali three times, and I have seen the beautiful temples in Yogyakarta. I have never been to Papua, but I have always wanted to go.
My friend Tom has traveled abroad. He has lived in Singapore for two years, and he has already visited Japan twice. I haven't been abroad yet, but I have saved some money for my first trip.
read.title: My Travel Experiences
